title: Myelodysplastic syndromes
subtitle: Clonal stem-cell disorders with ineffective hematopoiesis → cytopenias, dysplasia, and variable AML risk · blasts <20% · everything collapses to lower risk (fix the cytopenias) vs higher risk (alter the natural history)
source: Compiled from the Encyclopedia MDS review note and Fellowship Anki deck · WHO 2022 / ICC · IPSS-M (Bernard, NEJM Evid 2022) · Bernard/Papaemmanuil molecular taxonomy (Blood 2024)

blocks.heading: Diagnosis
items: Triad: (1) cytopenia + (2) morphologic dysplasia in >10% of a lineage + (3) clonality (cytogenetic or molecular). >90% show clonality on karyotype/NGS
Normal marrow cellularity ≈ 100 − age. Most MDS is hypercellular with ineffective hematopoiesis; a hypoplastic variant overlaps aplastic anemia
Dysplasia is not MDS without clonality. Exclude mimics first: B12, folate, copper deficiency, HIV, alcohol, medications, post-chemotherapy marrow recovery
† Hypoplastic MDS overlaps aplastic anemia and PNH — send flow for a PNH clone
† Consider VEXAS (somatic UBA1) in older men with inflammatory features, macrocytic anemia and vacuoles in myeloid and erythroid precursors

blocks.heading: Classification (WHO 2022 / ICC)
rows: At 10–19% blasts with a defining lesion, ICC calls it MDS/AML (managed as AML) while WHO calls it MDS-IB2
Macrocytic anemia, normal or high platelets, hypolobated megakaryocytes, female predominance

blocks.heading: Risk stratification
rows: Cytogenetic risk, marrow blast %, hemoglobin, platelets, ANC → 5 groups
Keeps blasts, Hgb, platelets, cytogenetics · drops ANC · adds 31 gene mutations → 6 groups
TP53-multihit highest risk · SF3B1 favorable · adverse: ASXL1, RUNX1, SRSF2, U2AF1, EZH2, FLT3, KMT2A-PTD
blocks.footnote: Calculator at mds-risk-model.com. IPSS-M still outperforms a purely molecular-subgroup model, so use it for risk scoring.

blocks.html:
Molecular taxonomy (Bernard/Papaemmanuil, Blood 2024). 3,233 patients, 152-gene panel → 16 molecular groups covering 86%, median OS ranging 0.9–8.2 years.

Favorable: SF3B1 (14%, most common, OS ~6 yr) · del(5q) · CCUS-like · ZRSR2 · driver-negative. Monocytic: bi-TET2 (13%, CMML overlap). Aggressive: AML-like (OS ~0.9 yr, 40% 2-yr AML transformation) · TP53-complex · IDH-STAG2 · −7/SETBP1 · EZH2-ASXL1 · BCOR. DDX41: high blasts and high transformation but no excess mortality.

Take-home: the prognostic weight of blast % depends on genetic subtype — but IPSS-M still outperforms a groups-only model, so the taxonomy informs biology rather than replacing risk scoring.

chains.header: Lower risk — goal is fixing cytopenias
Higher risk — goal is altering natural history
boxes: † timing driven by IPSS-M — do not wait for

blocks.heading: Biomarker / setting → therapy
rows: Lower risk, EPO <500, low transfusion burden
Luspatercept — activin receptor II ligand trap, improves late-stage erythropoiesis
Poor with everything → trial or transplant

blocks.heading: Trials
rows: The first RCT of azacitidine vs supportive care — higher response and delayed transformation to AML or death. The disease-modifying signal (Silverman, JCO)
Practice-defining — overall survival benefit in higher-risk MDS, median OS 24.5 vs 15 months (Fenaux, Lancet Oncol)

Improved response and delayed AML progression but no OS benefit. Caveat: decitabine was capped at 6 cycles (median 4) while azacitidine continued to progression (median 9). Practically, azacitidine is the HMA with an OS benefit
Lenalidomide in transfusion-dependent lower-risk del(5q) — ~67% transfusion independence (List, NEJM 2006)
Luspatercept after ESA failure, ring sideroblasts / SF3B1 — transfusion independence 38% vs 13%
Imetelstat in ESA-refractory non-del(5q) — 8-week transfusion independence 40% vs 15%
Donor vs no-donor in higher-risk MDS age 50–75 — 3-yr OS 47.9% vs 26.6%. The evidence for transplanting older patients (Nakamura, JCO 2021)
Venetoclax + azacitidine in higher-risk MDS missed its OS endpoint (22.2 vs 21.7 mo, HR 0.91) despite higher response rates — ven/aza is standard in AML but not MDS

Treatment pathway Lower risk — goal is fixing cytopenias Symptomatic anemia serum EPO <500 + low transfusion burden → erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (epoetin or darbepoetin) By biomarker isolated del(5q) → lenalidomide ring sideroblasts / SF3B1 → luspatercept ESA-refractory non-del(5q) → imetelstat Hypoplastic or younger immunosuppression: ATG ± cyclosporine Throughout transfusions; iron chelation if chronically transfused; infection prophylaxis Higher risk — goal is altering natural history Hypomethylating agent azacitidine (or decitabine) † give ≥4–6 cycles before judging response AZA-001: OS 24.5 vs 15 months Transplant-eligible allogeneic HSCT is the only cure † timing driven by IPSS-M — do not wait for AML transformation in higher-risk disease TP53-multihit poor with all standard therapy → prioritize clinical trial or transplant † After HMA failure dismal — clinical trial or transplant; no established standard salvage Biomarker / setting → therapy Setting Therapy Key trial Lower risk, EPO <500, low transfusion burden Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent — Lower risk, isolated del(5q) Lenalidomide MDS-003 / MDS-004 Lower risk, transfusion-dependent, ring sideroblasts / SF3B1 Luspatercept — activin receptor II ligand trap, improves late-stage erythropoiesis MEDALIST; COMMANDS (beat epoetin alfa first-line) Lower risk, ESA-refractory, non-del(5q) Imetelstat — telomerase inhibitor IMerge (FDA-approved 2024) Hypoplastic / younger lower risk Immunosuppression (ATG ± cyclosporine) — Higher risk Azacitidine or decitabine AZA-001 — OS benefit Higher risk, transplant-eligible Allogeneic HSCT — the only curative option — TP53-multihit Poor with everything → trial or transplant — Trials CALGB 9221 (2002) The first RCT of azacitidine vs supportive care — higher response and delayed transformation to AML or death . The disease-modifying signal (Silverman, JCO) AZA-001 (2009) Practice-defining — overall survival benefit in higher-risk MDS, median OS 24.5 vs 15 months (Fenaux, Lancet Oncol) † Decitabine (D-0007, EORTC 06011) Improved response and delayed AML progression but no OS benefit . Caveat: decitabine was capped at 6 cycles (median 4) while azacitidine continued to progression (median 9).
